title: Require 'outstanding' ratings for big Senior Executive bonuses
proposal: Top career executives in the Senior Executive Service should have to earn an 'outstanding' performance rating to receive large bonuses.
quote: An “outstanding” rating should be required for Senior Executive Service (SES) chiefs to win big bonuses

title: End or narrow the 'disparate impact' legal doctrine
proposal: The chapter says the legal idea of disparate impact, where results alone can suggest discrimination, could be ended by Congress or narrowed through regulations by a future administration.
quote: could be ended legislatively or at least narrowed through the regulatory process by a future Administration.

title: Bring back merit-based entrance tests for federal jobs
proposal: OPM should reform the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures so courts will revisit the old consent decree, and move forward with skills-based tests for hiring federal workers.
quote: A government that is unable to select employees based on KSA-like test qualifications cannot work, and the OPM must move forward on this very basic personnel management obligation.

title: Build political goals into career staff performance reviews
proposal: Political appointees should write policy goals directly into employee performance appraisals and take an active role in supervising reviews of career staff.
quote: It is essential that political executives build policy goals directly into employee appraisals both for mission success and for employees to know what is expected.

title: Use existing pay and awards to reward good performers
proposal: Until Congress creates a broader merit pay system, political leaders should use existing pay tools, especially cash awards, to reward good performance as far as the law allows.
quote: pay and especially fiscal awards strategically to reward good performance to the degree allowed by law.

title: Move EEOC's federal employee complaints unit to the MSPB
proposal: The EEOC office that handles federal employee discrimination complaints should be moved to the Merit Systems Protection Board, making the MSPB the main reviewer of firings and discipline.
quote: The EEOC’s federal employee section should be transferred to the MSPB

title: Return many Office of Special Counsel investigations to OPM
proposal: Many of the investigative duties of the Office of Special Counsel should be given back to OPM, to simplify the employee appeals process.
quote: and many of the OCS’s investigatory functions should be returned to the OPM. The MSPB could then become the main reviewer of adverse actions

title: Set federal pay by occupation and region using market data
proposal: OPM should set starting pay for each job type and region, track turnover and applicant numbers, and adjust pay based on that, which the chapter says mostly needs new laws.
quote: the OPM should establish an initial pay schedule for every occupation and region, monitor turnover rates and applicant-to-position ratios, and adjust pay and recruitment on that basis.

title: Make federal benefits equal to private-sector benefits
proposal: OPM should push for federal worker benefits to match those in the private sector, which the chapter says are less generous.
quote: Most of this requires legislation, but the OPM should be an advocate for a true equality of benefits between the public and private sectors.

title: Move federal pensions closer to private retirement plans
proposal: The chapter suggests considering further changes to make federal employee pensions more like private-sector retirement plans.
quote: it still remains much more generous, and other means might be considered in the future to move it even closer to private plans.

title: Hold regular GSA–OPM meetings on transitions and contractors
proposal: GSA and OPM leaders should meet regularly on shared issues, such as easing personnel limits during presidential transitions and how contractors relate to civil servants.
quote: it would make sense for GSA and OPM leadership and staff to hold regular meetings to work through matters of common interest

title: Freeze hiring for top career jobs at the start
proposal: At the start of the administration, hiring for all top career positions should be frozen so departing political appointees cannot move into permanent career jobs.
quote: What is needed at the beginning is a freeze on all top career-position hiring to prevent “burrowing-in” by outgoing political appointees.

title: Put performance first when deciding layoffs
proposal: In reductions-in-force, the President should insist that job performance be the top factor in deciding who keeps their job, ahead of tenure, veterans' preference and seniority, and avoid costly buyout-style cuts.
quote: A determined President should insist that performance be first and be wary of costly types of reductions-in-force.

title: Eliminate duplicate programs and cut functions
proposal: The chapter recommends finding and eliminating programs duplicated across departments, and cutting functions and budgets and shifting duties away from the federal government.
quote: A logical place to begin would be to identify and eliminate functions and

title: Reinstate Schedule F
proposal: Trump's Executive Order 13957, which created Schedule F to remove civil service hiring and firing protections from career employees in policy-related jobs, should be brought back, with Senior Executive Service accountability addressed first.
quote: at the demand of the civil service associations and unions. It should be reinstated, but SES responsibility should come first.

title: Enforce management rights in union bargaining
proposal: OPM and agency managers should again enforce the management rights written into law and not expand bargaining with federal unions.
quote: and should be enforced again by any future OPM and agency managements, which should not be intimidated by union power.

title: Reinstate Trump orders on federal unions and firing
proposal: The next administration should reinstate Executive Orders 13836, 13837, and 13839 on union contracts, union work on official time, and faster removal of poor performers, appoint an FLRA General Counsel, and restart the Impasses Panel.
quote: and should be reinstated by the next Administration, to include the immediate appointment of the FLRA General Counsel and reactivation of the Impasses Panel.

title: Congress to consider whether to allow federal employee unions
proposal: Congress should consider whether unions for public-sector workers should exist at all.
quote: Congress should also consider whether public-sector unions are appropriate in the first place.

title: Fill all political appointee jobs from the start
proposal: A new administration should have a full set of political appointees in place from the beginning, rather than relying on holdovers and career staff.
quote: it will need a full cadre of sound political appointees from the beginning if it expects to direct this enormous federal bureaucracy.

title: Give the OPM Director a seat in the Cabinet
proposal: The chapter says personnel should get top priority and recommends having the OPM Director available in the President's Cabinet so the President directly supervises the bureaucracy.
quote: it would make sense to give the President direct supervision of the bureaucracy with the OPM Director available in his Cabinet.
